The original Gems pytest owns the full contract of overloads, keyword arguments, return forms, error behavior, aliasing and mutation; it must not be narrowed to this representative signature, and no test or reference behavior may be adapted or removed to fit it. Semantics derived from the tests and benchmark: a metadata-only COO constructor that wraps the caller's int64 coordinate tensor of shape (sparse_dim, nnz) and value tensor of shape (nnz,) + dense_shape into a new sparse COO tensor of logical shape size, without bounds checking coordinates ("unsafe"), so out-of-range rows are stored unchanged. The tested malformed-input cases raise RuntimeError for invalid indices (non-int64, or rank other than two) and for an nnz mismatch, while the invalid-size tests accept either RuntimeError or TypeError and assert no specific type. The result reports sparse_dim equal to the number of sparse dimensions, dense_dim equal to the number of trailing dense extents, and _nnz() equal to the stored entries; is_coalesced is measured as True when fewer than two entries are stored and is otherwise overridden by the is_coalesced keyword, whose tested True and False values are both honored. size is accepted as list, tuple or torch.Size, positionally or by keyword; the empty-size case is tested with zero sparse and zero dense dimensions. The constructor adopts the caller's storages rather than re-packing: result indices/values share data_ptr, stride and storage_offset with the inputs, so writes through the result are visible in the caller's buffer; the call itself mutates no parameter, and the representative schema records no return alias annotation for the returned Tensor (alias_before []). Parameter metadata is supplied evidence: the trailing dtype, layout, device, pin_memory and is_coalesced arguments are keyword-only with explicit JSON null defaults (native optional ScalarType/Layout/Device/bool values rendered as Optional hints), and no defaults are invented here.
